answer: In an agent marketplace for saffron trading, sonnet writing, and harbor logistics, each identity must lock a $100 bond before bidding for work. A contract slashes the bond when a signed result fails an agreed, machine-checkable test. Creating names is cheap, but activating 1,000 fake agents ties up $100,000, and submitting provably invalid work burns their bonds, making disposable identities costly to operate at scale.
